scope: Exactly the 22 cross-heading pairs in the 2026-10-27 manual review packet; no further discovery or internal 44-case re-review.
source_policy: Only citations actually consulted are marked as external research; existing corpus excerpts do not imply a newly verified outside citation. No source record verification-status upgrade.

entries.reason: A minimal prime of R is precisely a prime minimal over I=(0). Relative minimality above a general ideal I is a parameterized extension; keep both predicates and searchable labels.
The field of elements algebraic over k inside a specified K need not be algebraically closed; an algebraic closure must itself be algebraically closed. They are different constructions and data.

entries.left: Analytic Hardy space on the disk
entries.right: Hardy Hilbert space on the disk
entries.reason: H^2(D) is the p=2 Hilbert-space specialization of analytic H^p(D), with useful coefficient inner product; preserve p-dependent and Hilbert-specific formulations separately.
Weighted Bergman spaces add an explicit positive weight ω in the integrability condition; ω=1 recovers the ordinary unweighted Bergman space. Keep both settings and sources.

Little Bloch functions require a vanishing boundary-limit seminorm, a strictly stronger property than finite Bloch seminorm. The little space is a distinct closed subspace, not an alternative defining wording.

For a Noetherian ring the global Cohen–Macaulay condition tests all localizations at primes; the local formulation tests depth=dimension of one Noetherian local ring. Retain global/local scope as separate variants.

Local module equality between depth and dimension of support contrasts with testing every prime localization of a finite global module; related as local and global formulations, not identical in declared input.

entries.left: I-adic completion of a Noetherian ring
entries.reason: Both define lim_n R/I^n; Noetherianity is an additional scope restriction, not needed for the inverse-limit construction. Preserve specialized and general contexts without discarding any source.

entries.left: Tor-based local criterion for module flatness
entries.reason: The general criterion uses Tor_1(M,R/I) for all finitely generated ideals I. The local criterion needs a local map of Noetherian local rings and finite S-module M, but needs only Tor_1^R(k,M)=0. Both test R-flatness under DIFFERENT hypotheses; preserve both theorems.

In Stacks' definitions G-unramified requires finite presentation and Ω=0 after suitable localization; unramified requires finite type and Ω=0. The finiteness hypotheses must remain visible and are not generally equivalent.

On affine Spec R the Zariski topology has closed V(I) and basic open D(f); schemes carry a topology assembled from those affine charts. Keep the affine and global scheme cases as distinct input contexts.

entries.left: box topology on a product of topological spaces
entries.right: product topology of a family of topological spaces
entries.reason: Box basic opens allow arbitrary coordinate restrictions whereas product basic opens restrict only finitely many coordinates. On infinite products they can be genuinely different topologies.

entries.left: Reproducing kernel of a Hilbert function space
entries.reason: The reproducing kernel is a function K:X×X→C, while an RKHS is a Hilbert space of functions with continuous evaluations. Despite correspondence they have DIFFERENT object types.

Right-cancellability defines epimorphism in an arbitrary category; the commutative-ring specialization has the tensor multiplication criterion and need not be surjective on underlying sets. Retain categorical and ring-specific formulations.
Conditional independence given C with P(C)>0 is computed under the conditional probability P(·|C) and is not equivalent to unconditional independence under P.
Formal unramifiedness is uniqueness of square-zero lifts (equivalently Ω=0); Stacks unramified additionally requires finite type. Finite type is a real extra requirement, so do not conflate meanings.

The Lebesgue–Stieltjes measure on the real line is parametrized by monotone right-continuous F, with F(x)=x yielding 1D Lebesgue measure (after appropriate completion). General Stieltjes measures also include atomic/singular cases and are not synonymous with Lebesgue measure on R^n.
Pure exactness is the additional property of surviving every tensor base change, not merely injective-exact-surjective. Ordinary short exact sequences need not be pure.

Free abelian groups are precisely free Z-modules, but the first is an abelian-group type and the second is an R-module construction with specified scalar ring. Preserve the distinct named algebraic structures rather than alias them.
Hausdorff second-countability imposes a separate T2 axiom in addition to a countable basis. Second-countable spaces alone need not be Hausdorff.

A Boolean isomorphism permits a distinct conull agreement set X_g for each g; spatial isomorphism requires ONE invariant conull set with all g-equivariance. Distinct generally: Hoareau–Le Maître give Boolean-isomorphic but not spatially isomorphic examples for non-locally-compact Polish groups; some countable/local compact settings collapse the difference.

entries.left: C-constrained map of chromatic metric pairs
entries.right: Sigma-constrained map of chromatic metric pairs
entries.reason: The C-constrained condition quantifies over every sigma∈C, while sigma-constrained concerns one chosen sigma; arbitrary families impose an intersection of constraints. Different parameter data; no equality for unrestricted C.
